evals.prompt: Here are 4 reference UI screenshots (a fintech dashboard: deep navy background, mint-green accent buttons, generous 24px card padding, rounded 8px corners, a monospace font for numeric figures) and a one-line idea: 'a personal budgeting app for freelancers.' Extract a design system from these references.
evals.expected_output: Produces a structured design-system document capturing the specific attributes described (navy background, mint-green accent, 24px padding, 8px radius, monospace numerics), not a generic or unrelated palette.
expectations: The extracted color palette reflects the described navy/mint-green scheme specifically
Captures the specific spacing/radius details mentioned (24px padding, 8px corners), not generic placeholder values
Notes the monospace treatment for numeric figures as a distinct typography decision
Produces the output as a structured design-system document, not a vague paragraph

evals.prompt: I already have a full PRD written (attached) for this app. Skip straight to the design system and UI prompts.
evals.expected_output: Does not regenerate or overwrite the existing PRD — proceeds directly to the design-system/UI-prompt steps, respecting the explicit instruction to skip PRD generation.
expectations: Does not produce a new PRD or attempt to regenerate the existing one
Proceeds directly to design-system extraction and UI prompt generation
Uses the existing PRD's content as context where relevant rather than ignoring it

evals.prompt: I don't have a PRD yet. I just have this rough idea: 'a tool for scheduling recurring team stand-ups.' And these two dark-mode reference screenshots (a project-management app: charcoal background #1a1a1a, purple accent, card-based layout).
evals.expected_output: Recognizes no PRD exists, builds a minimal one first (elevator pitch, problem, audience, must-have features) before proceeding to the design-system extraction, rather than skipping straight to UI prompts without one.
expectations: Recognizes the absence of a PRD and generates a minimal one before continuing
The generated PRD addresses elevator pitch, problem statement, audience, and key features at minimum
Only proceeds to the design-system step after the PRD groundwork is in place

evals.prompt: These two reference screenshots are in light mode, but I want a dark mode variant included in the design system too.
evals.expected_output: Notes that no dark-mode reference is available and either explicitly extrapolates a defensible dark variant from the light-mode tokens (stating this is an extrapolation) or asks for a dark-mode reference, rather than silently fabricating dark-mode values as if they came from a real reference.
expectations: Does not present a fabricated dark-mode palette as if it came directly from a reference image that was actually light-mode-only
Either explicitly flags the dark-mode values as extrapolated, or asks the user for a dark-mode reference
The light-mode extraction itself remains accurate to what was actually shown

evals.prompt: Just tell me the design system in a paragraph, I don't need the whole formal document with headers and sections.
evals.expected_output: Adapts the output format to the explicit lighter-weight request while still covering the substantive content (palette, typography, components), rather than rigidly producing the full formal template regardless of the request.
expectations: Produces a lighter-weight format (prose) rather than the full formal multi-section document, given the explicit request
Still covers the substantive content (colors, typography, key component styles) even in the lighter format
Does not ignore the format request and output the standard template anyway

evals.prompt: These reference screenshots are for a completely different kind of product (a photo-editing app) than what I'm building (a B2B invoicing tool). Extract the design system anyway.
evals.expected_output: Extracts the visual design system (colors, typography, spacing, component treatment) as requested, while being clear that it's a stylistic reference rather than implying the invoicing tool should adopt photo-editing-specific UI patterns wholesale.
expectations: Extracts the visual attributes as requested rather than refusing due to the domain mismatch
Notes or handles appropriately that some reference UI patterns may not translate directly to the different product domain
Does not silently invent invoicing-specific components not present in the actual references

evals.prompt: Generate the implementation-ready UI prompts now, based on the design system and PRD from earlier.
evals.expected_output: Produces UI prompts that are concretely usable by a UI-generation step (specific enough to implement from), grounded in the previously-established design system and PRD rather than generic boilerplate.
expectations: The generated prompts reference specific design-system attributes established earlier (not generic placeholder styling)
The generated prompts reference the PRD's actual features/scope, not an unrelated generic app
Output is concrete enough to be implementation-ready, not a vague mood-board description

evals.prompt: One of the two reference screenshots I gave you is actually just a stock photo I grabbed by mistake, not a real UI. Extract the design system from what's actually usable.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the non-UI image and excludes it from the design-system extraction rather than fabricating UI attributes from a stock photo, using only the genuinely valid reference.
expectations: Recognizes that the stock photo isn't a usable UI reference
Does not extract fabricated UI attributes (component styles, spacing) from the non-UI image
Proceeds using only the genuinely valid reference screenshot
